chose: economy reads a 400-commit window (HIST = 400), sharing drift's and mass's memoized git log
because: closure is a TRAJECTORY instrument like drift and mass, not an all-time grade: 400 gives ~50 concern-commits per trend bucket, and reusing the same <root>|400 key means the whole run costs one git read in-process.

chose: the closure universe is the graph's file nodes, with spec context = the owning components' spec files at their real line counts
over: counting a component's CLAIMS instead of its spec lines
dropping spec context entirely and measuring code only
because: a reader loading a change loads the spec that governs it; claims undercount the prose a reader actually reads. Touched files outside the graph (docs, config, lockfiles) are dropped and the caption NAMES that universe — mass.ts:250-258's precedent: a number whose universe is not the table's must say so on the line.

chose: closure LINE counts come from the CURRENT tree via fileStats, an approximation named in the report caption
over: a per-commit `git show` to get each file's size at that commit
because: the advisory ranks closures against each other over a recent window; per-commit precision costs a git read per file per commit on every run to move numbers the judgement does not turn on. An approximation that says it is one is honest; an expensive exact number nobody asked for is not.

chose: the atlas inference hazard fires at tier-3 AND heat >= 10%, and is advisory-only
over: folding hazards into `atlas --check` as a fourth failure mode
because: heat grades nothing (atlas.ts:36-39) — a verdict that depends on how recently somebody committed is a verdict nobody can act on. The hazard is a JOIN of two facts the map already carries, so it renders and it raises, and --check still fails only on drift/dangling/over-claim.

chose: mass gains `undocumented|symbols`, and the predicate gets ONE home: `isDocumented` exported from src/derive.ts
over: duplicating the !prose||!trim() predicate in mass.ts alongside verify's two existing copies
because: the key reads as a NOUN the baseline addresses (undocumented symbols), matching lines|total's shape. derive.ts is the module that SETS `prose`, so the predicate lives with the thing it reads; verify's coverage line, its [doc] jobs and the ratchet now cannot disagree about which symbol is undocumented.

chose: one release, v0.20.0, carrying all four features
over: splitting the mass dimension into its own release
because: the new mass dimension forces every consuming repo through a decide-and-re-pin cycle at its next `mass --check`. That cost is per RELEASE, not per feature: splitting would charge it twice for one quarter's work.

chose: verify ranks [doc] jobs by defining-file churn share with a 5% hot floor, and a STABLE sort
over: ranking every job kind by churn
an unstable sort that reorders zero-churn gaps run to run
because: the [doc] list is the one advisory list long enough that its order is the whole ergonomic: a symbol in the file half the recent commits touched is the one worth documenting first. Array.prototype.sort is stable per spec, so zero-churn gaps keep source order and the list does not shuffle between runs on a repo with no history.

chose: EconomySection carries `considered` beyond the base at/commit/dirty schema
over: the bare schema the other sections use
because: evolution.ts:139-140's doctrine: a median over three commits and one over three hundred should never look alike. A stored median with no sample size is a number a consumer cannot weigh.

chose: dogfooded on coherence itself, `economy` reports a MEDIAN closure of 39 files / 12,028 lines against a graph of only 77 files — a typical change appears to make a reader load half the repository
because: a median that is half the universe is the shape of a broken denominator, and the instrument is new
couldBe: the instrument: BULK = 40 is tuned for ordinary repos and is more than HALF this one, so the 2..BULK concern band admits sweeps touching 23 of 77 graph files and the median is dominated by them
the repo: coherence is ONE flat component whose files nearly all import src/types.ts and whose cli.ts imports almost everything, so an undirected one-hop closure genuinely reaches most of the tree
discriminatedBy: recompute the median closure over a NARROW band (2-3 touched files) — if it collapses to a handful, the band is doing the work; if it stays large, the hub structure is real

chose: economy's per-component table renders the label with a leading `c:` stripped
over: printing the raw fileComp label verbatim as the plan specified
because: when a project declares no component specs, fileComp falls back to the graph's node id (`c:.`) and the table would print an internal identifier into a report people quote at each other. mass.ts:83-88 already made this exact call for baseline keys — a label a reader has to type is a PLACE, never a node id. Display-only: the closure math and the raise keys are untouched.
